question: What is the recommended duration for exclusive breastfeeding according to global health standards?

options.A: The first six months of life
options.B: The first twelve months of life
options.C: The first nine months of life
options.D: The first three months of life

explanation: Global guidelines state that infants should receive only breast milk for the first six months to ensure optimal growth, development, and health. [learn more](BMP214_U3_T3#BMP214_U3_T3_h1)

question: Why is giving plain water to an exclusively breastfed two-month-old discouraged?

options.A: It destroys all the maternal antibodies already stored in the infant's liver
options.B: It causes immediate permanent damage to the baby's developing kidneys
options.C: It fills the infant's stomach and can introduce pathogens or reduce breast milk intake
options.D: It permanently stops the mother from producing any more breast milk

explanation: Breast milk contains all the water an infant needs, even in hot climates. Giving extra water takes up limited stomach space and risks introducing contaminated water. [learn more](BMP214_U3_T3#BMP214_U3_T3_h1)

question: Name the specific substance produced in the first few days after birth that is packed with antibodies.
explanation: Colostrum is the first milk produced after birth, often called the baby's first immunization due to its high concentration of protective antibodies. [learn more](BMP214_U3_T3#BMP214_U3_T3_h2)

question: Which major protective agent is abundant in breast milk to line the baby's gut against infections?
explanation: Secretory IgA is an antibody that survives the baby's digestive tract to line the mucous membranes, blocking bacteria and viruses from entering the body. [learn more](BMP214_U3_T3#BMP214_U3_T3_h2)

question: Which two international organizations jointly launched the Baby-Friendly Hospital Initiative?
explanation: The United Nations Children's Fund and the World Health Organization created the BFHI in 1991 to promote best practices in maternity facilities. [learn more](BMP214_U3_T3#BMP214_U3_T3_h3)

question: What was the main goal of establishing the Baby-Friendly Hospital Initiative globally?

options.A: To replace traditional birth attendants with certified pediatric surgeons
options.B: To stop hospitals from using practices that discourage or disrupt breastfeeding
options.C: To provide free commercial infant formula to every mother giving birth
options.D: To train mothers how to manufacture their own breast milk substitutes

explanation: The initiative targets hospital routines—like unnecessary separation and early formula use—that interfere with successful breastfeeding establishment. [learn more](BMP214_U3_T3#BMP214_U3_T3_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the Ten Steps to Successful Breastfeeding?

options.A: Providing routine afternoon formula top-ups to all large babies
options.B: Enabling mothers and infants to remain together twenty-four hours a day
options.C: Training all healthcare staff in the skills necessary to implement the policy
options.D: Facilitating immediate and uninterrupted skin-to-skin contact at birth

explanation: Routine formula supplementation is explicitly discouraged under the Ten Steps unless there is a clear, documented medical indication. [learn more](BMP214_U3_T3#BMP214_U3_T3_h4)

question: Why is rooming-in emphasized as a core component of baby-friendly maternity care?

options.A: It prevents the infant from developing any form of neonatal jaundice
options.B: It allows the mother to learn feeding cues and feed her baby on demand
options.C: It guarantees that the mother will experience zero postpartum blues
options.D: It lowers hospital electricity bills by reducing nursery lighting needs

explanation: Keeping the baby by the mother's side twenty-four hours a day promotes frequent feeding and strengthens the maternal-infant bond. [learn more](BMP214_U3_T3#BMP214_U3_T3_h4)

question: What is the primary underlying cause of sore and cracked nipples in a breastfeeding mother?

options.A: Failure to apply commercial lanolin cream before every single feed
options.B: A natural physiological drop in maternal estrogen levels after delivery
options.C: Washing the breasts with clean water too frequently during the day
options.D: Incorrect positioning and poor attachment of the baby to the breast

explanation: When a baby only latches onto the nipple instead of taking a large part of the areola into the mouth, trauma and cracking occur. [learn more](BMP214_U3_T3#BMP214_U3_T3_h5)

question: A mother on day two postpartum says her breasts feel rock-hard and swollen, and her baby cannot get a good latch. What is the best initial nursing action?

options.A: Advise her to stop breastfeeding immediately and give formula for two days
options.B: Help express a small amount of milk to soften the areola so the baby can latch
options.C: Apply tight chest binders to suppress the painful swelling and milk production
options.D: Reassure her that this is completely normal and requires no intervention

explanation: Engorgement makes the areola too tight for a proper latch. Expressing a little milk softens the tissue, enabling the infant to attach correctly. [learn more](BMP214_U3_T3#BMP214_U3_T3_h5)

question: Why is it important for midwives to involve family members, such as grandmothers and husbands, in breastfeeding counseling?

options.A: They take over all physical household chores while the mother is lactating
options.B: They hold significant influence over home-based infant feeding decisions and practices
options.C: They are responsible for purchasing all commercial infant formulas required
options.D: They are legally required to sign consent forms for the baby's immunizations

explanation: In many communities, older relatives and spouses guide domestic health choices. Engaging them helps secure crucial family backing for exclusive breastfeeding. [learn more](BMP214_U3_T3#BMP214_U3_T3_h6)

question: Which strategy is most effective for sustaining exclusive breastfeeding after a mother leaves the hospital?

options.A: Community support groups and timely postpartum follow-up visits
options.B: Providing a free can of infant formula as a backup plan at discharge
options.C: Encouraging her to isolate herself from family advice completely
options.D: Sending automated text messages reminding her to stop at six months

explanation: Ongoing community support and prompt follow-up help mothers troubleshoot early challenges and resist pressure to introduce other foods. [learn more](BMP214_U3_T3#BMP214_U3_T3_h6)
